items.title: the tooltip for a MACRO is upgraded - a derive name in `[derive(Storable)]` (kolt account.vl:9:9) answers `macro fun Storable(item: Item): Source` today, the signature every derive shares and which says nothing a reader wants; and the import leaf `Storable` in `import std::reactive::store::{ Storable, Store };` (account.vl:2:32) names BOTH the trait and the derive macro of that name, and the tooltip should say so - what the derive WRITES, the trait it implements with its `///`, where it lives, and the macro's own doc
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-10-12/13): "upgrade the tooltip for macros (account.vl:2:32 and account.vl:9:9)"; the pins `macro_attribute_hover_and_definition` and `prelude_derive_definition_reaches_std` (document.rs ~21590: the hover contains `macro fun PartialEq(item: Item): Source`, the definition lands on the macro fun); std `store.vl` `export macro fun Storable(item: Item): Source` beside `store_core.vl` `export trait Storable` (the same name, two facets); E149 (hovering a derived equality answers with the GENERATED eq - the generated code is reachable from the hover); G29 (export of a macro inside a mod); E298/E299 (the `mod` line, the import-segment hover); E238 (a header line above the fence); B264 (an alias hovers with its target's signature); B613 (the Storable steer)
items.body: (1) A derive name in `[derive(X)]`: one fence - `mod std::reactive::store` (E299's line), then what the derive writes for THIS item: `impl Account with Storable` (the generated impl's head, from the expansion the analyzer already holds - E149's door; for a derive that writes several impls, one line each), then the trait's head and its `///` as the Doc block (the trait is what the reader is opting into; `Storable`'s doc says what a store diffs by), then the macro's own `///` (if any) and a SignatureNote `derive macro: macro fun Storable(item: Item): Source` so the macro facet stays visible and go-to-definition's target is named. A derive whose generated code is REFUSED (a dyn member, G25) leads with the refusal (E213's rule). A user `macro fun` used as an attribute (`[derive_tag]`) answers its signature and `///` as today, plus the `mod` line. (2) An import leaf that names a trait AND a derive macro: the trait's block (head, members, `///`) first, then a line "Also a derive macro: `[derive(Storable)]`" with the macro's doc; an import leaf naming only a macro: the macro's signature and doc; the same for a bare macro reference. (3) A `macro fun` CALL site (`tabled!`-style, a `macro` invocation): its signature, `///`, and `mod` line - unchanged in substance, upgraded in shape. Pins: the kolt derive (a std derive over a user struct - the generated impl line), a prelude derive (`PartialEq`), a user macro attribute (the existing pins stand), the two-facet import leaf, a macro-only leaf, a refused derive. Sizing S (vilan-lsp document.rs; the expansion's impl heads from the analyzer's macro tables).
